editorial:
Behind Office Doors is a 1931 RKO Radio Pictures drama. William LeBaron produced it and Melville W. Brown directed. Mary Astor plays Mary Linden, a private secretary. The picture ran 82 minutes and was released under the working title 'Private Secretary'. It was adapted from Alan Schultz's 1929 novel of that name, with a screenplay by Carey Wilson and adaptation and dialogue by J. Walter Ruben. Creators will find it as an early-sound office melodrama with a recognizable cast, and copies are on the Internet Archive.

The rights question is renewal. A film released in 1931 was protected for 28 years and needed a renewal filing in 1958 or 1959 to continue. Wikipedia says no renewal was filed, but I could not verify that in the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes or the Copyright Office records. Until you check those, do not treat the print as cleared. The Internet Archive's public-domain label is the uploader's claim, not a rights finding. The underlying novel's status has also not been checked.
faq: Can I use Behind Office Doors in a video or documentary?

Not yet with confidence. Wikipedia reports that the 1931 copyright was not renewed, but I did not confirm that in the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes or the Copyright Office public records. Search those yourself first. The Internet Archive's public-domain label is only the uploader's claim.
Does the Internet Archive copy settle the rights?
No. The uploader marked it public domain, but that is not a rights determination. The novel 'Private Secretary' (1929) and any music in the soundtrack have also not been checked.
